review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no simp attributes and no simp-set-sensitive rewrites, only `simpa only [...]` calls with explicit lemma lists, so there is no loop, competing-rule or unwanted-expansion issue. I checked the sibling CoefficientIdeal.lean and found that `comap_map_C` and `map_C_le_map_C_iff` are already @[simp]. I also checked the downstream use in PrimaryDecomposition.lean, which names `isPrimary_map_C_iff` explicitly in `simp only`. The one finding is a possible missing simp attribute on `isPrimary_map_C_iff`. It is a judgment call and rests on source reading only. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested whether the attribute causes any simp failure or conflict.

findings.problem: This is the canonical normalisation lemma for `(I.map C).IsPrimary`. Its left side is `Ideal.map C I` with `I` a variable, and its right side is the smaller expression `I.IsPrimary`. The rewrite therefore terminates and is not ambiguous. Neither `σ` nor the ring hypotheses appear on the right, so the lemma is unconditional. The sibling lemmas about the same `Ideal.map C` pattern, `comap_map_C` and `map_C_le_map_C_iff`, are @[simp], but this iff is not. As a result, goals that mention primaryness of an extended ideal are not reduced by plain `simp`. The one in-repo simp use, in PrimaryDecomposition.lean, has to name the lemma by hand.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the theorem @[simp], placing the attribute before the docstring or declaration the way `comap_map_C` does in CoefficientIdeal.lean. The orientation can stay as it is. Both `Ideal.map C I` and `IsPrimary` are fixed, and no existing simp lemma rewrites `(Ideal.map C I).IsPrimary` in another way. If the authors prefer not to enlarge the global simp set, the alternative is to leave it unmarked and document that callers should pass it to `simp only`.
findings.benefit: Plain `simp` would then reduce `(Ideal.map C I).IsPrimary` to `I.IsPrimary` in the same way it already reduces `comap C (map C I)` and `map C I ≤ map C J`. Users would not need to import or name the lemma, and the simp interface for `Ideal.map C` would be consistent across `CoefficientIdeal.lean` and `Primary.lean`.
